question: The ratio of 'mass by volume percentage' to 'volume by volume percentage' of a given solution gives ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**density of solute**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'mass by volume percentage' represents the **mass of the solute per 100 mL of the solution**.
 
• 'Volume by volume percentage' represents the **volume of the solute per 100 mL of the solution**.
 
• The ratio of 'mass by volume percentage' to 'volume by volume percentage' provides the **density of the solute** because density is defined as mass per unit volume.
 
• This relationship is derived from the formula: **Density = Mass / Volume**.
 
• It is important to note that this calculation assumes the volume of the solute is used directly in the denominator without considering solution interactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Density:** Density is a physical property defined as mass per unit volume, commonly expressed in units like g/mL or kg/m³.
 
• **Mass by Volume Percentage:** It is calculated as (mass of solute / volume of solution) × 100, representing the concentration of a solution.
 
• **Volume by Volume Percentage:** It is calculated as (volume of solute / volume of solution) × 100, often used for liquid-liquid solutions.
 
• **Solute and Solvent:** In a solution, the solute is the substance dissolved, while the solvent is the medium in which the solute is dissolved.
 
• **Applications:** Understanding density and concentration is crucial in fields like chemistry, biology, and material sciences for solution preparation and analysis.
